newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UCB optimistic on Zyrtec in U.S., Japan.
newsitem.headline: UCB optimistic on Zyrtec in U.S., Japan.

text.p: Belgian chemicals, drugs and films group UCB said on Wednesday it expected registration in Japan of its star anti-allergy drug Zyrtec by the end of this year and sales would start immediately afterwards.

In the U.S., where the product has been on sale since February 1996, chief executive officer Georges Jacobs foresaw full year 1997 sales of "probably" $200 million after a better than expected $140 million in the partial year 1996.

He told a news conference on provisional 1996 results that Zyrtec had contributed to a "a nice increase" in ordinary profit in the pharma sector to 3.4 billion francs in 1996 from 2.7 billion in 1995.

A 30 percent rise in group pre-tax profits before exceptionals had been "helped" by royalties from sales of Zyrtec in the U.S., he said. After less than a year the cost of setting up the sales organisation there had already been recouped.
In the U.S. UCB has a marketing agreement with Pfizer under which 85 percent of sales goes to Pfizer, UCB books 15 percent and gets a 12 percent royalty.
Jacobs said the deal would be negotiated this year with UCB counting on raising the royalty to 25 percent.

UCB was considering setting up a Zyrtec production facility in the U.S. next year to cope with expected saturation at its production facility near Brussels, where an epilepsy drug is also due to come on stream next year.

In Japan UCB has a co-promotion agreement with Sumitomo. "We are too small to start from scratch." But after six years UCB would take over handling sales, Jacobs said, adding Japan "will represent a nice contribution to growth in the pharma sector."
Jacobs expected "a big increase (in profit contributions) in Japan from 1998." The market in Japan was favourable with a "fantastic" increase in allergies due to "pollution of all sorts."
